_comment: The simulation timeline - one authored week on the board. Each day activates or resolves events that already live in scenarios.json; nothing is duplicated here, because a second copy of an event is how schema parity breaks. Days carry state forward: a shipment rerouted on Tuesday is ON the new route on Wednesday, and a held one accrues a day of delay for every day it waits.
_honesty: Every event and every day here is authored. The Route Advisor still makes each decision for real - the timeline only decides which disruptions are active when. This is a replay, and the dashboard tags it SCRIPTED.
name: One week on the North Range
summary: A quiet Monday, a walkout, a river running low, a corridor closing, and then the slow climb back. Eight days, five disruptions, one pool of shipments.

days.label: Mon
days.headline: Quiet start
days.note: Nothing active. Every booking is running to plan - this is the baseline the rest of the week moves away from.

days.label: Tue
days.headline: Hamburg walkout called
days.note: The union calls a full-day stoppage across the container terminals. Boxes with slack move to Rotterdam; the tight cold-chain one is better off waiting.

days.label: Wed
days.headline: The Rhine falls with the strike still on
days.note: Low water at Kaub cuts barge drafts while Hamburg is still stopped. Two unrelated disruptions at once is the case a single-event demo never shows.

days.label: Thu
days.headline: Red Sea closes - the week's worst day
days.note: A corridor closure lands on top of both. Every lane on the board is now touched by something.

days.label: Fri
days.headline: Hamburg settles; the hold releases
days.note: The stoppage ends. The shipment held since Tuesday resumes - carrying the delay it accrued while it waited, which is the cost of that call made visible.

days.label: Sat
days.headline: Wildfire closes a land leg
days.note: A regional fire shuts the inland route south. Small, contained, and it only touches one booking - the system should not treat it as a board-wide event.

days.label: Sun
days.headline: The river comes back, the fire is contained
days.note: Two of the four clear. What is left is the corridor closure, which does not resolve in a week.

days.label: Mon
days.headline: Settled on the revised plan
days.note: The Red Sea stays shut. Everything still moving is doing so on a route the system chose earlier in the week. One booking is still waiting, because no better routing exists for it - saying so is a real answer, not a gap.
